speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo; to help me understand your condition, could you please describe what these episodes feel like and how long they typically last?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. The fact that your dizziness is position-dependent and causes a spinning sensation is very helpful. Are these episodes accompanied by any other symptoms, such as hearing loss, tinnitus, ringing in the ears, or trouble speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The classic presentation of position-dependent vertigo without auditory symptoms in an elderly patient strongly supports this diagnosis. I would like to confirm this with a Dix-Hallpike maneuver.
